db_evidence.notes: Text-only retrieval (semantic_search/run_sql) reliably narrowed the general vicinity of all 4 boss encounters -- episodes rows near 17000s, 17400s, 28850-28920s and 52080-52260s all describe the relevant dragon/loong boss content (verified directly with memcli sql). But the exact short spoken/subtitled line that answers the question is not faithfully captured anywhere: (1) the offline episodes captions themselves misread the subtitle differently at each window (e.g. 17400-17430 caption reads '无量前，天也要变何似？', 28860-28890 caption records an 'incoherent' whisper fragment '和暗服清背何故 是约西', 52230-52260 records only a fragment '却因果'); (2) clip_qa calls at the same 17399-17460 window across two different rollouts (and even two calls within the same rollout) each produced a different transcription, none matching the reference; (3) direct frame extraction and 6-8x upscaling by this diagnosis at clue_interval #1 (17004-17067, the window no rollout ever visited) still leaves the on-screen subtitle too small/blurred to confidently OCR by inspection. This points to a genuine source-fidelity limitation (small stylized wuxia-style subtitle text at the video's resolution/compression) rather than a simple 'agent didn't look' failure, compounding the retrieval-location misses.

root_causes: 3 of 5 rollouts (1, 3, 4) never queried any of the question's 4 clue_intervals with clip_qa at all -- their text search located the right general chapters but then drifted to a different, thematically-similar dragon scene (a different boss onset, a backstory monologue) and spent their one visual-verification call confirming the wrong scene.

2 of 5 rollouts (0, 2) did land clip_qa correctly on clue_interval #2 (17399-17460), but neither ever checked clue_interval #1 (17004-17067), the chronologically earliest window and the most likely candidate for 'the first line' as literally asked.

Where clip_qa did probe a correct window, its OCR/transcription of the on-screen Chinese subtitle was unstable: repeated calls on the identical or overlapping time range in the same or different rollouts produced mutually inconsistent readings, and none matched the reference's beheading/marketplace imagery.

The underlying episodes-table captions (built once, offline) also misread this subtitle differently at each of the 4 windows, suggesting the source video's small stylized subtitle text is close to the OCR limit of the captioning/vision pipeline at this resolution -- a source-fidelity ceiling, not merely an agent laziness/search issue.

None of the 5 rollouts cross-checked their candidate answer against all 4 clue_intervals to confirm the SAME line recurs before each of the 4 battles (which the question's phrasing implies), which would have been a natural way to disambiguate a correct vs. hallucinated reading.
what_worked: Text-only retrieval (semantic_search over event_steps/episodes plus run_sql date-range scans) consistently located the correct rough time regions for the 4 boss encounters across all 5 rollouts, including rollout 3 and 4 which ran SQL directly over all 4 correct ranges before drifting away from them.

Rollout 0's clip_qa did land on one真 clue window (17399-17460) and produced a reading in the right thematic family ('without cause, why...'), earning partial (1/5) credit from the judge even though the exact wording was wrong.
transferable_lessons: For 'first line before N events' questions with multiple given clue windows, visit and clip_qa EVERY clue interval, especially the chronologically earliest one, before submitting -- do not stop at the first plausible-looking window found.

When a candidate line is supposed to recur before several separate encounters, cross-verify the SAME line appears in at least two of the clue windows before trusting a single clip_qa read; a stable reading across independent windows is much stronger evidence than one call.

Treat inconsistent clip_qa transcriptions of the same on-screen text (across repeated calls) as a signal that the subtitle is at the OCR resolution limit -- worth requesting a tighter crop/zoom or multiple frames rather than accepting the first free-form transcription.

Don't let a 'plausible flavor match' (a different dragon-themed line found nearby) substitute for verifying it falls inside one of the question's actual clue intervals; check the timestamp against the given windows before committing to it as the answer.
open_questions: Whether the reference-answer's exact wording ('Without cause, why should a head be hung in the marketplace?') is genuinely spoken at clue_interval #1 (17004-17067) -- this diagnosis could not confirm it by direct frame inspection since the subtitle remained illegible even at 8x upscale; it was inferred only from the DB's noisy caption fragments ('无有因' pattern, '却因果' fragment) sharing the 'cause' (因) theme.

Whether this is in fact a single recurring taunt line reused before all 4 loong mini-boss fights (as the question's phrasing implies) or 4 distinct lines, one per encounter -- if the latter, the question/reference may be under-specified about which of the 4 is intended as 'the first line'.
Why rollout-02 attempt-1 crashed (error.json) -- not inspected in this diagnosis since attempt-2 completed and was scored.
